title: Chapter XXX
summary: Jane forms with Diana and Mary the effortless intellectual and emotional companionship she has never known. St. John remains apart, devoted to duty but driven by restless ambition and a missionary resolve that offers power more than peace. Before the sisters return to poorly paid governess positions, he offers Jane a cottage and thirty pounds a year to teach poor girls at Morton. She accepts the small, honest independence. News then arrives that the Riverses' wealthy uncle John has left his twenty-thousand-pound fortune to one other relation rather than to them.
events: Jane, Diana, and Mary develop strong mutual affection through study, conversation, and art.
Jane perceives unquiet ambition beneath St. John's austere ministry and learns of his missionary plan.
St. John offers Jane the Morton village-school position, which she accepts.
The Rivers siblings learn that Uncle John has left almost his entire fortune to another relative.

characters.name: Jane Eyre
characters.development: Finds both chosen sisterhood and a modest vocation that restores economic autonomy.

characters.name: Diana and Mary Rivers
characters.development: Become Jane's first fully congenial female companions but must return to dependent governess work.

characters.name: St. John Rivers
characters.development: Channels frustrated appetite for action and power into a severe ideal of missionary duty.

threads.text: St. John provides Jane with independent employment as a village schoolmistress.
St. John prepares to sacrifice home and emotional ties to missionary ambition.
A wealthy Uncle John has left twenty thousand pounds to an unnamed relation instead of the Rivers siblings.
